title: High-frequency traders dominate most stocks, making them difficult for retail traders to profit from
claim: High-frequency traders dominate most stocks, making them difficult for retail traders to profit from. Day traders should focus on 'Stocks in Play'—stocks with unusual volume or volatility anomalies that break free from HFT control temporarily.
support: Direct statement on market microstructure; practical advice for retail market selection

title: Day trading is buying and selling a security within the same trading day to profit from intraday pri
claim: Day trading is buying and selling a security within the same trading day to profit from intraday price movements. Retail day traders must comply with Pattern Day Trader (PDT) rules and maintain minimum $25k account equity.

title: The three-step rule limits risk: (1) Never risk more than 2% of account equity on a single trade, (2
claim: The three-step rule limits risk: (1) Never risk more than 2% of account equity on a single trade, (2) Position size accordingly using stop-loss distance, (3) Exit immediately upon hitting stop-loss—no exceptions.
support: Core risk management discipline; foundational principle throughout book

title: Risk Management
claim: Traders who adhere strictly to 2% max loss per trade have fewer catastrophic drawdowns and longer survival in live trading
mechanism: Position sizing discipline reduces exposure to tail risk

title: Starting account size should be at least $25,000; begin with smaller position sizes and scale up onl
claim: Starting account size should be at least $25,000; begin with smaller position sizes and scale up only after proving profitability over months

title: Stocks in Play have high relative volume (3–10x daily average), recent news catalysts, and prices ty
claim: Stocks in Play have high relative volume (3–10x daily average), recent news catalysts, and prices typically $1–$30. Float <50M and market cap <$500M preferred for volatility.

title: The rationale for selecting low-float, high-volume stocks is to find temporary supply/demand imbalan
claim: The rationale for selecting low-float, high-volume stocks is to find temporary supply/demand imbalances that retail traders can exploit before institutions rebalance.
support: Logical extension of market microstructure chapter

title: Biotech and small-cap tech stocks exhibit the highest intraday volatility; energy and healthcare als
claim: Biotech and small-cap tech stocks exhibit the highest intraday volatility; energy and healthcare also provide consistent opportunities.
support: Author's trading experience and book examples

claim: A professional day trading platform must support: Level 2 order book, hotkeys for rapid entry/exit, real-time stock scanners with volume filters, and sub-100ms order latency.
support: Technical requirements for executing book's strategies

claim: Use gap scanners (overnight gaps >5%), volume radar (rel vol rank >8), and pre-market movers lists to build daily watchlists of Stocks in Play.

title: Key patterns: doji (indecision), hammer (reversal candidate), engulfing (trend change), morning/even
claim: Key patterns: doji (indecision), hammer (reversal candidate), engulfing (trend change), morning/evening stars (reversal signals). Reliable on 5-minute and higher timeframes.

title: ABCD: Stock rises (A->B), pulls back (B->C) to 50-61.8% Fibonacci, breaks above B (C->D) on breakout
claim: ABCD: Stock rises (A->B), pulls back (B->C) to 50-61.8% Fibonacci, breaks above B (C->D) on breakout. Entry at D on breakout, stop below C.

title: ABCD Pattern Entry
claim: ABCD breakout entries with stop below C have positive expected payoff (reward >=2x risk) on 5-min charts for high-volume stocks
mechanism: Reversal of pullback suggests trend resumption

title: Bull flag: stock rallies sharply, forms consolidation (flag) on lower volume, breaks out above flag
claim: Bull flag: stock rallies sharply, forms consolidation (flag) on lower volume, breaks out above flag on volume. Entry on breakout, stop below flag low.

title: Reversal: stock falls sharply on low volume, rallies back (reversal candle) on sudden volume spike.
claim: Reversal: stock falls sharply on low volume, rallies back (reversal candle) on sudden volume spike. Enter at break of reversal high, stop below low.

title: 20-day and 50-day MA crossover on daily chart signals longer-term trend; 5-min 9-EMA and 20-EMA cros
claim: 20-day and 50-day MA crossover on daily chart signals longer-term trend; 5-min 9-EMA and 20-EMA crossover confirms intraday entry timing.

title: VWAP acts as intraday support/resistance. Bounce entries at VWAP on high volume; breaks below sugges
claim: VWAP acts as intraday support/resistance. Bounce entries at VWAP on high volume; breaks below suggest trend weakness.

title: VWAP Support
claim: Bounce entries at VWAP on 5-min chart with volume >2x average have expected payoff >=1.5x risk
mechanism: VWAP as fair-value; bounces = mean reversion

title: Support/resistance levels from daily or hourly chart provide reliable entry triggers on intraday bre
claim: Support/resistance levels from daily or hourly chart provide reliable entry triggers on intraday breaks. Retry entries form on recovery after testing support.

title: Red-to-green: stock gaps down, rallies back through opening, breaks above to turn green. Entry on br
claim: Red-to-green: stock gaps down, rallies back through opening, breaks above to turn green. Entry on break above opening with stop at gap low.

title: ORB: note opening range (first 5-15 min), breakout above range high/below range low signals momentum
claim: ORB: note opening range (first 5-15 min), breakout above range high/below range low signals momentum continuation. Entry on confirmed breakout.

title: Disciplined workflow: (1) Build watchlist (7-9 AM), (2) Plan entries/exits before market open, (3) E
claim: Disciplined workflow: (1) Build watchlist (7-9 AM), (2) Plan entries/exits before market open, (3) Execute per plan, (4) Exit at first target or stop-loss, (5) Review day for lessons.

title: The workflow structure enforces systematic risk control by separating decision phases (plan) from ac
claim: The workflow structure enforces systematic risk control by separating decision phases (plan) from action (execution), reducing emotional bias and revenge trading.
support: Author's discipline emphasis + behavioral finance principles

title: Avoid revenge trading, overconfidence after wins, and wishful thinking. Patience and strict rule adh
claim: Avoid revenge trading, overconfidence after wins, and wishful thinking. Patience and strict rule adherence are more important than finding the perfect trade.
support: Repeated psychological warnings in early chapters

title: Traders fail by: (1) ignoring stop-losses, (2) averaging down into losers, (3) holding winners too l
claim: Traders fail by: (1) ignoring stop-losses, (2) averaging down into losers, (3) holding winners too long, (4) taking trades outside planned setup.

title: Fundamental analysis (P/E, earnings, balance sheet) is less useful for day traders; focus on technic
claim: Fundamental analysis (P/E, earnings, balance sheet) is less useful for day traders; focus on technical/momentum signals. Catalysts trigger gaps but do not determine minute-to-minute moves.

title: Most volatile stocks trade in pre-market (4-9:30 AM) and first hour after open (9:30-10:30 AM). Afte
claim: Most volatile stocks trade in pre-market (4-9:30 AM) and first hour after open (9:30-10:30 AM). Afternoon trading less active. After-hours has low liquidity.

title: Use market orders for entries (quick fills), limit orders for exits (protect against slippage). Unde
claim: Use market orders for entries (quick fills), limit orders for exits (protect against slippage). Understand partial fill risk in low-liquidity names.

title: The book provides a structured framework: stock selection filters, nine pattern-based strategies, ri
claim: The book provides a structured framework: stock selection filters, nine pattern-based strategies, risk discipline, and execution workflow. Prescriptive but lacks quantitative backtests and expected-return estimation.
